source_derived_workflow_rules.source_meaning: Use this kit after being served with a Petition when disputing one or more Petition claims or making claims of your own.
The kit states a 30-day deadline to serve and file a response to a Petition.
Form 15-19B Notice of Intent to Answer may provide 10 additional days according to this source; a written agreed extension is another source-described path.

If a Notice of Application was also served and the user wishes to respond, the source directs the user to a separate kit and states application-response material must be served/filed at least seven days before the hearing.
The source describes mandatory early dispute resolution after the Answer or Answer and Counter-Petition is filed, subject to emergency/family-violence/abduction exemption paths.

For a later interim application dealing with children, the source says Parenting after Separation and Divorce registration is required before the application is heard and recommends early attendance where child claims exist.

If the Petition does not claim divorce but the Counter-Petition will, the source requires a marriage certificate or Certificate of Registration of Marriage and describes translation requirements where applicable.

Use Form 15-19A Answer when the Petition contains all issues that need resolution and the respondent disputes how they should be resolved; use Form 15-20 Answer and Counter-Petition when the respondent needs to add claims not already made.
If either party claims child or spousal support, the source generally requires Form 15-47, subject to source-described agreement/waiver exceptions.
If either party claims division of family property, the source requires Form 15-49, subject to a source-described waiver exception.
If the Counter-Petition adds a support claim that the Petition did not contain, the source requires service of Form 15-51 with the Counter-Petition.
The source instructs the user not to sign Financial or Property Statements early and requires signing/sworn-or-affirmed completion before a Commissioner for Oaths.
For an Answer without Counter-Petition, the source describes multiple service methods and proof paths depending on recipient and method.
The source says an Answer and Counter-Petition must be personally served on the Petitioner, even when represented, by someone other than the Respondent.
The source describes acknowledgment, personal-service affidavit and alternate-mode affidavit paths, but contains form-number discrepancies that block clean normalization.
After service, the source directs filing originals plus proof of service and lists filing fees that must be treated as stale/unverified until current official comparison.
The source describes negotiation/dispute resolution, possible interim applications, and eventual pre-trial/trial paths when issues remain unresolved.

observed: The table of contents, service instructions and checklist call the Acknowledgment of Service Form 12-13.
The embedded form heading is Form 12-3 (Subrule 12-3(1)).
Most instructions, checklist and embedded form identify Affidavit of Personal Service as Form 15-8A.
One Answer and Counter-Petition service instruction calls it Form 15-18A.
The artifact is dated 2023-04-10 and contains deadlines, filing fees, dispute-resolution rules and service instructions.
